title: deprecate-x-project-token-prefix-and-align-ephemeral-scope-headers-for-streaming-toolcalls
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: Streaming tool/function-calling paths and the OpenAI compatibility layer had diverged semantics around project-scoped tokens and per-stream proof headers. This caused intermittent 401s during long-lived streaming tool calls (especially when tokens rotated) and inconsistent CORS behavior for browser-originated streaming sessions. This PR consolidates the runtime and compat layers behind an ephemeral, canonical header contract and deprecates the older project-token prefix behavior.

What this change does (high level):
- Introduces a transient header X-Redwood-Ephemeral-Scope that carries scoped token metadata (scope id, expiry, hmac) in a compact base64 form. This header is honored on streaming handshakes and toolcall preflight requests.
- Adds X-Redwood-Stream-Proof for per-connection integrity checks (short-lived HMAC of the handshake). The runtime validates this on accept and rejects if mismatch or expired.
- Updates the OpenAI-compat mapping layer (openai_compat) to translate legacy Authorization: Project <token-prefix> into the new ephemeral-scoped handshake when the gateway can mint/upgrade tokens, with a best-effort migration path.
- Deprecates the behavioral reliance on prefix-based project tokens in the gateway and documents the migration. The prefix still accepts but logs a deprecation metric and a warning header to clients.
- Harmonizes CORS preflight acceptance for the new headers: OPTIONS now returns Access-Control-Allow-Headers including X-Redwood-Ephemeral-Scope and X-Redwood-Stream-Proof, and adds explanatory Access-Control-Expose-Headers for the structured-output advisory header.
- Adds a small structured-output advisory header X-Redwood-Structured to signal that the model endpoint returned JSON-LD style structured sections. This helps browser clients avoid early text-only parsing heuristics.

Compatibility and rollout strategy:
- Backward compatible: gateways will continue to accept legacy Project-prefixed Authorization for 30 days after rollout; during that window they automatically exchange for an ephemeral scope token when possible.
- Canary-first: change gated behind feature flag runtime.ephemeral_scope_enabled. We will enable on 10% of traffic for 48 hours, monitor auth error rate, stream disconnects, and latency regressions.
- Migration docs and quickstart added (docs/migration/project-scoped-to-ephemeral.md) explaining SDK changes required for client-side token refresh and handshake renewal.

Tests and validation:
- Unit tests for header parsing and HMAC validation added (runtime/streaming/handshake_test).
- Integration test for streaming toolcall lifecycle with token rotation simulated (perf-canary/streaming-auth-rotate.yml).
- E2E smoke against openai_compat endpoints ensuring header translation and CORS preflight acceptance.

Rollout checklist (included in description to aid reviewers):
- [x] Add header parsing and validation logic
- [x] Implement compat translation path with explicit logging for legacy tokens
- [x] Add CORS allowed/expose headers for streaming flows
- [x] Add migration docs and SDK example update (js/python)
- [x] Add metrics: auth.legacy_token_usage, auth.ephemeral_handshake_failures, stream.handshake_latency
- [x] Canary rollout + monitor

Why not a cookie or existing Authorization-only flow: cookies are fragile for cross-origin streaming and add CSRF surface; existing Authorization flows lacked a standard short-lived handshake that binds the connection to the token lifecycle (causing out-of-band token rotation races). The ephemeral header + stream-proof HMAC gives an accountable, per-connection contract without affecting bearer semantics for non-streaming REST calls.

Notes on SDK changes: JS and Python SDKs gain a helper that performs a background handshake refresh and replaces the X-Redwood-Ephemeral-Scope header before a long stream reaches 70% of the scope expiry. Example code snippets live under redwood-sdk-typescript/examples/ephemeral-handshake.

Related: ENG-9342 (stream stability), ENG-9410 (openai compat header mapping), SUP-8471 (support case: repeated 401 on long streams).
commits:
* 9 changesets:
  - add ephemeral scope header parsing and validation (runtime/streaming/handshake.rs)
  - implement stream-proof HMAC verification (runtime/crypto/stream_proof.rs)
  - openai_compat: map legacy project prefix to ephemeral upgrade path (api/openai_compat/headers_mapping.go)
  - update CORS handling and expose structured advisory header (http/cors/middleware.go)
  - add migration docs and SDK example (docs/migration/project-scoped-to-ephemeral.md, redwood-sdk-typescript/examples)
  - add unit/integration tests and CI job update (ci/pipelines/streaming-auth.yml)
  - metric instrumentation and dashboard query (observability/dashboards/ephemeral-auth.json)
  - remove direct reliance on project-token-prefix usage in gateway (gateway/auth/legacy_bridge.go)
  - update CHANGELOG and release notes
review_thread:
Liam O'Connor: Can we avoid parsing large base64 blobs in the hot path? Suggest sending a short derived id and server-side lookup.

Maya Chen: Updated to include a compact id + server lookup fallback. The handshake still accepts compact id or full compact-b64; decoding only happens when proof verification is required. See runtime/streaming/handshake.rs commit.

Priya Nair: How does this affect WebSocket proxying paths (we have a proxy that strips some headers)?

Maya Chen: Added a middleware to re-inject required ephemeral headers when proxy injects an X-Forwarded-Auth token (gateway/auth/legacy_bridge.go). We also added a diagnostic metric for headers-stripped-by-proxy.

Evan Patel: CI lint failed on first run (go vet on headers_mapping). It looks fixed in the follow-up commit.

Maya Chen: Yes, fixed; CI now passes.

Liam O'Connor: Approve after canary and docs updates.

Priya Nair: Approve.

Evan Patel: Approved (non-blocking comments addressed).
release_notes:
- Introduce X-Redwood-Ephemeral-Scope and X-Redwood-Stream-Proof headers for streaming handshakes and tool/function calls.
- Deprecate prefix-based Project tokens for streaming flows (legacy accepted during migration window).
- CORS preflight now allows and exposes new streaming headers.
- SDKs updated with handshake refresh helpers (see migration doc).
notes_for_ops: Enable runtime.ephemeral_scope_enabled=false initially. Prepare Canary 10% rollout, observe metrics: auth.ephemeral_handshake_failures (target <0.1%), stream.disconnect_rate (no regression), auth.legacy_token_usage (drop over time). Alert on >1% handshake failure over 15m.
changelog_entry: Feature: Ephemeral streaming auth headers and OpenAI-compat translation for project tokens (runtime + api)
